newsitem.title: USA: TCF to merge with Winthrop Resources.
newsitem.headline: TCF to merge with Winthrop Resources.

text.p: TCF Financial Corp said Friday it had signed a letter of intent to acquire Winthrop Resources Corp, a leasing company, in a deal valued at about $326 million.
Shareholders of Minneapolis-based Winthrop will receive one share of TCF for every 1.2877 shares of Winthrop, TCF said.
The deal is expected to close by the end of the second quarter, the companies said.
TCF said it had suspended its share repurchase program as a result of the pending merger.
Winthrop, with leased assets of $327 million, specializes in leasing high-tech and business equipment. This is a new business line for TCF, the company said.
"This is a well-managed, dynamic firm that will increase our asset origination capacity and complement our existing lines of business," TCF Chief Executive William Cooper said in a news release.
After the merger, Winthrop will become a subsidiary of TCF Bank Minnesota, the companies said.
The deal values Winthrop at $36.50 a share, based on a TCF stock price of $47, TCF said.
TCF shares were down 7/8 at 46-1/4 and Winthrop shares were unchanged at 34 at midday Friday.

The merger is subject to negotiation of a definitive agreement, satisfactory completion of due diligence review, approval by both companies' boards and shareholders, required regulatory filings and approvals, and treatment of the transaction as a pooling of interests for accounting purposes, they said.
TCF is a $7.1 billion asset stock savings bank holding company with banking operations in Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin, Michigan and Ohio.
